title: How In Vitro Fertlization Works
summary: Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant explain in vitro fertilization (IVF): its history starting with Louise Brown in England in 1978, US and global birth numbers, success rates by age, preimplantation genetic diagnosis (PGD), infertility definitions, low-tech fertility treatments such as Clomid and artificial insemination (including intrauterine insemination and sperm washing), the five-step IVF process (ovarian stimulation, egg retrieval, insemination/ICSI and fertilization, embryo culture, embryo transfer), GIFT and ZIFT alternatives, risks such as ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome, cost and insurance coverage state laws, and freezing eggs or embryos. The episode closes with listener mail from Paul Roney, a luthier who was disciplined for working on guitar designs on the clock after his employer captured screenshots.

segments.title: Opening banter and IVF history
segments.summary: Hosts open with off-topic movie chat, then introduce IVF, Louise Brown as the first test tube baby in England, and the spread of IVF births since 1978 and 1979.

segments.title: IVF success rates and live birth
segments.summary: Discussion of IVF success rates by age in the US, the meaning of live birth per cycle, and a study linking IVF births to higher rates of major birth defects.

segments.title: PGD, selective reduction and ethics
segments.summary: Explanation of preimplantation genetic diagnosis for monogenic disorders and its cost, along with ethical concerns and selective reduction of multiple pregnancies.

segments.title: Defining infertility
segments.summary: The hosts define infertility as a year of unprotected intercourse without pregnancy, note that doctors vary in practice, and cite an estimate of about 6.1 million Americans facing infertility.

segments.title: Low-tech treatments: Clomid and artificial insemination
segments.summary: Clomid as an oral ovulation-inducing drug with its success rates over three cycles, including a suspended NFL player who used it for fertility. Artificial insemination is explained, including intrauterine insemination and why sperm must be washed.

segments.title: The IVF process: stimulation, retrieval, fertilization
segments.summary: Costs and insurance variation, then the five steps of IVF: ovarian stimulation with hormones, egg retrieval by transvaginal aspiration or laparoscopic surgery, insemination and fertilization in culture, and embryo development over several days.

segments.title: Embryo transfer, risks, and alternatives
segments.summary: Embryo transfer by catheter, chemical pregnancy and ectopic pregnancy, physical and emotional risks including ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome, and alternatives GIFT and ZIFT, plus ICSI and egg freezing.

segments.title: Insurance mandates and state laws
segments.summary: Many insurers treat IVF as elective, while about fifteen states require coverage of infertility treatment; Massachusetts is mentioned as a state with strong coverage and expert doctors.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts wrap up, direct listeners to further reading on the website.
